'''Georg Müller''', [[Congregation of the Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary|SS.CC.]] (7 June 1951 – 25 October 2015) was the [[Bishop]] of the [[Roman Catholic Territorial Prelature of Trondheim]], which encompasses central sections of [[Norway]], from 1988 to 1997.

==Biography==
Müller was born in [[Volkesfeld]], Germany. He completed his early education in [[Lahnstein|Lahnstein am Rhein]] in 1971.<ref name=apobit/> He made his simple vows with the [[Congregation of the Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary]], known as the Arnsteiner Fathers, on 28 July 1972, and completed his training at the order's theological seminary in 1977. He was ordained to the priesthood on 18 March 1978 in [[Simpelveld]] in the Netherlands by his predecessor in Trondheim Bishop {{Interlanguage link|Gerhard Schwenzer|de}}. He graduated from the [[University of Münster]] in 1981.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|archive-url= https://archive.today/20120524153243/http://www.katolsk.no/biografier/innenriks/gmueller |title= Georg Müller | website= Den katolske kirke| url-status=live|archive-date= 24 May 2012 | access-date=6 August 2018 | url= http://www.katolsk.no/biografier/innenriks/gmueller | language=no}}</ref>

In 1981, he began his pastoral work in Trondheim as a parish priest, became vicar general in 1984, and a parish pastor in 1997.<ref name=apobit/> [[Pope John Paul II]] named him Apostolic Administrator of Trondheim on 9 February 1988 and then Prelate of Trondheim on 20 June 1997.<ref name=bio/> He received his episcopal consecration there on 28 July 1997 from Cardinal [[Edward Cassidy]].<ref name=bio /> As the leader of the church in Trondheim, he was successful in recruiting sisters from several orders to work in Norway.<ref name=apobit/>

==Sexual abuse==
[[Pope Benedict XVI]] accepted his resignation on 8 June 2009, when he was 58, citing the provision of [[Canon Law]] that a bishop can resign if unable to fulfil his office.<ref name=reuters>{{cite news |title=Corrected: Norwegian bishop who resigned in 2009 was abuser |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pope-abuse-norway/corrected-norwegian-bishop-who-resigned-in-2009-was-abuser-idUSTRE6362KE20100407 |access-date=6 August 2018 |work=Reuters |date=7 April 2010}}</ref> The normal retirement age for a bishop is 75. Speculation in the media attributed his removal to internal problems within the local Church administration.<ref name=SZ/>

On 7 April 2010, the Norwegian daily newspaper ''[[Adresseavisen]]'' reported that Müller had resigned following allegations of sexual abuse 20 years earlier.<ref name=adressa20100407>{{cite news |title=Biskop tilsto sexovergrep mot altergutt |language=no |work=Adresseavisen |url=https://www.adressa.no/nyheter/innenriks/2010/04/07/Biskop-tilsto-sexovergrep-mot-altergutt-1106345.ece |access-date=6 August 2018 |date=7 April 2010 |archive-date=1 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180801124729/https://www.adressa.no/nyheter/innenriks/2010/04/07/Biskop-tilsto-sexovergrep-mot-altergutt-1106345.ece |url-status=dead }}</ref> The report was confirmed by Catholic Church officials in Norway, and a spokesperson for the [[Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith]] confirmed that the abuse of a boy had been reported to Church officials in January 2009. It said Müller had undergone therapy and was no longer engaged in pastoral work. The accuser chose to remain anonymous, and due to the statute of limitations, no legal action could be pursued.<ref name=adressa20100407/><ref name=reuters/> Müller's removal came after Church officials had followed a review process that included a determination by a priest appointed by the Bishop of Stockholm that the charge was credible, a referral to the Vatican by Archbishop Emil Paul Tscherrig, the Apostolic Nuncio to Norway, and a final determination of guilt by a three-judge panel.<ref name=adressa20100407/> A spokesperson for the Catholic Church in Norway said that in 2009, "The official explanation was that the bishop had problems cooperating with others in the church, but that was only a part of the truth. The reason for not coming out with everything was that the victim did not want that."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wakin |first1=Daniel J. |title=Abuse Case Forced Bishop in Norway to Quit in '09 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/04/08/world/europe/08church.html |access-date=6 August 2018 |work=New York Times |date=7 April 2010}}</ref> Oslo Bishop [[Bernt Ivar Eidsvig]] said: "Müller has been divested of his authority, and he won't be allowed to work in a church again. He will never again be given a position in the church."<ref>{{cite news |title=Church: Norway Bishop Resigned over Sex Abuse |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/church-norway-bishop-resigned-over-sex-abuse/ |access-date=6 August 2018 |work=CBS News |date=7 April 2010}}</ref> The man who accused Müller thanked the Church for confirming his allegations and for the support it had provided him.<ref>{{cite news |title= Overgrepsoffer takker kirken |language= no |work= Adresseavisen |url= https://www.adressa.no/nyheter/trondheim/article1477968.ece |access-date= 6 August 2018 |date= 3 May 2010 |first= Sæba |last= Bajoghli |archive-date= 7 August 2018 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20180807032515/https://www.adressa.no/nyheter/trondheim/article1477968.ece |url-status= dead }}</ref> Media coverage was extensive in Norway and included reports that Müller was celebrating Mass in public at a hospital in Germany. Bishop Eidsvig called that "improper and impermissible" and said he would pursue the matter.<ref>{{cite news| access-date= 6 August 2018 | url= http://www.newsinenglish.no/2010/04/08/disgraced-bishop-still-holding-mass/ | work= New in English from Norway | date = 8 April 2010 | title= Disgraced bishop still holding mass}}</ref> In Germany, officials at the hospital and the local diocese said they had not been informed of any charges against Müller.<ref name=SZ>{{cite news |last1=Wiegand |first1=Ralf |title=Ex-Bischof fliegt nach Missbrauch auf |url=https://www.sueddeutsche.de/politik/katholische-kirche-in-norwegen-ex-bischof-fliegt-nach-missbrauch-auf-1.18514 |access-date=6 August 2018 |work=Süddeutshce Zeitung |date=9 April 2010 | language=de}}</ref> The Church reportedly later paid a settlement of over 400,000 krone.<ref name=adressa20130820/>

In an interview with ''[[Byavisa]]'', a local Trondheim newspaper, in August 2013, Müller denied there had been any abuse. He said that his departure from Trondheim was misinterpreted as an admission of guilt when he had only left to avoid the media. He stated that a German clinic in [[Osnabrück]] had confirmed that he was never a pedophile. Müller had sought without success to retract his statements before publication. The newspaper also reported that he appeared not to be supervised in any way, despite the Vatican's commitment that he would be.<ref name=adressa20130820>{{cite news |title=Müller hevder han aldri tilsto overgrep |language=no | work=Adresseavisen  |url=https://www.adressa.no/nyheter/trondheim/article8131423.ece |access-date=6 August 2018 |date=20 August 2013}}</ref> Bishop Eidsvig said Müller's statement showed bad judgment and that Müller had confessed in 2009. He doubted Müller would attempt to have the Vatican rehabilitate him.<ref>{{cite interview |title=Viser Müllers dårlige dømmekraft |language=no | work=Adresseavisen  |url=https://www.adressa.no/nyheter/article8131415.ece |access-date=6 August 2018 |date=20 August 2013|first=Berit |last=Baumberger }}</ref>

In retirement, he lived at his order's residences, first in Rome and then in Münster. He died in Münster on 25 October 2015. The obituary published online by his order did not mention the reasons for his resignation. It said that "he bore his suffering with composure and patience".<ref name=apobit>{{cite web| title= Nachruf Georg Müller SSCC | language=de | date= October 2015| website= Arnsteiner Patres }}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url= https://www.adressa.no/nyheter/trondheim/2015/10/26/Georg-M%C3%BCller-er-d%C3%B8d-11731055.ece | work= [[Adresseavisen]] | title= Georg Müller er død | access-date= 6 August 2018 | date= 26 October 2015 | language= no | archive-date= 7 August 2018 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20180807033954/https://www.adressa.no/nyheter/trondheim/2015/10/26/Georg-M%C3%BCller-er-d%C3%B8d-11731055.ece | url-status= dead }}</ref>

Muller was not replaced in Trondheim until 2019. Bishop Eidsvig was named Apostolic Administrator when Muller's resignation was accepted in 2009, and he served until 2019 when [[Erik Varden]] was nominated as his successor.
